newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy's orimulsion plant to come onstream soon.
newsitem.headline: Italy's orimulsion plant to come onstream soon.

text.p: Italian electricity firm ENEL is to start commercial burning of Venezuelan company Bitor's trademark fuel orimulsion at the Brindisi South power station in September, a senior Bitor official said on Friday.
Daniel Ramirez-Isava, president of London-based Bitor Europe Ltd, said the company would start sending regular 80,000-tonne shipments of orimulsion to Italy later this month.
Some 500,000 tonnes of orimulsion will be burnt at the plant over about six months as a test before any long-term deal is signed, Ramirez-Isava told Reuters.
He was speaking in the margins of a conference on trade and investment opportunities in Venezuela's energy and petrochemicals sectors, organised by the Belgian Foreign Trade Board.
Ramirez-Isava said the brand new plant would burn about two million tonnes a year of orimulsion if the final negotiations were successful.
Orimulsion is a controversial fuel that some environmentalists say is extremely dirty, although Bitor denies this.
It is a suspension of naturally occurring bitumen in about 30 percent water and contains toxic heavy metals which Bitor says can be recovered efficiently without escaping into the air.
ENEL has been aiming to reduce its heavy reliance on fuel oil for electricity generation, partly for environmental reasons, and sees orimulsion and natural gas as alternatives.

Britain's new Labour government decided in June not to consider renewing imports of orimulsion until it had conducted a public inquiry into plans by National Power Plc to convert its 2,000-megawatt Pembroke plant in south Wales to the fuel.
Until last year Britain burnt orimulsion at two PowerGen Plc plants but these have now been closed because they were not equipped with flue gas desulphurisation (FGD) equipment.
The Pembroke plant should be fitted with FGD equipment that would remove 94 percent of sulphur dioxide emissions from the combustion gases, according to Bitor.
If the go-ahead for the power station is given -- the public inquiry could last up to two years -- it could burn four to five million tonnes of orimulsion a year.
Bitor is holding talks on supplying orimulsion to Sardinia, Turkey, Germany, Greece, the Netherlands and China.
Denmark is currently Europe's biggest importer of orimulsion, consuming 1.5 million tonnes a year. Other importers include Canada and Japan.
Bitor is a subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA).
